assessments.reasoning: The last paragraph of answer 24 names the compiled library and both headers, classifies the combination, and directs marking of changes in zlib.h.
Conditions 2 and 3 explain the significance of altered source and source distribution. Classification of the specific package comes from the FAQ.
The annotated v1.4 tag targets the commit serving the inspected FAQ. It establishes the release context alone. Signature verification reports bad_email.

challenge.method: Tested the claim against three cases separately: an altered library with both headers, an unchanged library with both headers, and a compiled library supplied alone.
challenge.results: The publisher’s classification covers the two-header combination, and its alteration instructions address changes that were actually made. The passage supplies no direction to invent change markings for an unchanged copy. Removing both headers from the hypothetical removes a stated premise of the FAQ example. Its reasoning cannot establish a binary-only classification or an exemption from every condition.

limitations: This is the publisher’s view of the named combination. The FAQ passage leaves binary-only, one-header and other combinations unclassified. No actual shipment was inspected.
reasoning: FAQ 24 explicitly classifies a compiled zlib library supplied with both zlib.h and zconf.h as a source distribution. In its discussion of alterations, it directs the distributor to change both version definitions and record the origin and nature of changes in zlib.h.
